recipe/problem: A store path is named by what went into it. So before Nix can name a build, every input has to be written down.
recipe/recipe: That written-down recipe is a derivation. You make one by calling a function, also named derivation, with an attribute set.
recipe/name: The name goes on the end of the store path.
recipe/system: The system says what kind of machine can run this build. Here, it is the one you are on.
recipe/builder: The builder is the program to run, and args are what it gets. Here a shell runs one line.
stages/eval: Evaluate that, and nothing gets built. Nix writes the recipe into the store, as a file ending in dot D R V. That step is called instantiating.
stages/know: And Nix already knows the output path. It comes from the recipe, so there is no need to wait for a result.
stages/none: That path has a name, but nothing is there yet.
stages/realise: The second stage is called realising. It runs the recipe, and fills in that path.
build/out: The builder has to put its result somewhere. Nix hands it the path in a variable called dollar out, and the builder must write there.
build/sealed: The build runs sealed off, in what Nix calls a sandbox. On Linux, that is the default.
build/no: It has no network. It cannot see your home folder, or slash user slash lib.
build/only: It sees the store paths the recipe declares, and a temporary folder to work in.
build/trust: Nothing went into the result that the recipe does not name. That is why a path named from the recipe can be trusted.
string/need: Now a second recipe needs the output of the first. Import reads another file and gives back its value, and here that value is the first derivation.
string/insert: Insert a derivation into a string with a dollar sign and braces, and you get its output path.
string/context: But the string also carries something you cannot see: a note that it depends on that derivation. Nix calls this string context.
string/record: Hand that string to a new recipe, and the note becomes part of it. Ask the new dot D R V what it depends on, and there is the first one.
string/order: So Nix knows to realise hello first and world second, and nobody had to tell it.
